column1: # The AD104 B7/B8/B9 calibration matrix. PROPOSED: B7, B8, and B9 are read out
# of the llama.cpp source rather than supplied, and
# evidence/ada/b789-calibration-design.md states the derivation, the confound,
# and what confirming it would take.
# B is ne11: the number of columns of the second operand of a quantized
# mat-mul, which for a prefill of N tokens inside one ubatch equals N. It is not
# the logical batch, the ubatch size, or a compile-time constant.
# ggml_cuda_mul_mat consults ggml_cuda_should_use_mmvq before
# ggml_cuda_should_use_mmq, and on GGML_CUDA_CC_ADA_LOVELACE (890, this device)
# mmvq.cu:295-306 reads: Q2_K MMVQ at ne11 <= 4, Q3_K <= 6, Q4_K and Q5_K <= 7,
# everything else <= MMVQ_MAX_BATCH_SIZE, which mmvq.cuh:3 sets to 8. Above its
# threshold a type falls to ggml_cuda_should_use_mmq, which returns true at
# mmq.cu:312 for every NVIDIA part at Turing or later. Seven, eight, and nine
# therefore bracket the two thresholds this device carries: Q4_K and Q5_K leave
# MMVQ between B7 and B8, Q6_K between B8 and B9.
# MMVQ multiplies through packed __dp4a; MMQ on a Turing-or-later part takes the
# integer mma path. The math column names that consequence rather than a second
# measurement.
# Arms are ordered by B rather than by artifact, so one artifact's three B
# values sit maximally far apart in the sequence and a monotone drift across the
# campaign cannot present as a B effect. The runner repeats the opening arm last
# as the closing control.
# arm_id
b7-q4k

column14: Q4_K at 61.11% of bytes and Q6_K at 38.36% both on MMVQ, so the artifact is about 99.5% MMVQ by byte
